title: Octupole-driven spin torque switching of antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions
title_zh: 八极驱动的反铁磁隧道结自旋转矩开关
abstract: Magnetic tunnel junctions based on ferromagnets are canonical devices in spintronics, with wide-ranging applications in data storage, computing and sensing. They simultaneously exhibit mechanisms for electrical detection and control of magnetic order through the tunnelling magnetoresistance (TMR)1–5 and spin-transfer torque6–9 effects, respectively. It was long assumed that neither of these effects could be sizeable in all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions (AATJs), considering that they have no net magnetization. However, it was recently shown that AATJs based on chiral antiferromagnets do exhibit TMR due to their non-relativistic momentum-dependent spin polarization and cluster magnetic octupole moment, which are manifestations of their spin–split band structure10–13. However, the reciprocal effect, that is, the antiferromagnetic counterpart of spin–transfer torque, has been assumed non-existent due to the total electric current being spin-neutral. Here we report nanoscale AATJs that display this reciprocal effect, which we term octupole-driven spin-transfer torque (OTT). We demonstrate current-induced OTT switching of PtMn3|MgO|PtMn3 AATJs, with a TMR value of 363% at room temperature and switching current densities of the order of 10 MA cm–2. Our theoretical modelling explains the origin of OTT in terms of the imbalance between intra- and inter-sublattice spin currents across the AATJ, and, equivalently, in terms of the non-zero net cluster octupole polarization of each PtMn3 layer. This work establishes a new materials platform for antiferromagnetic spintronics and provides a pathway towards deeply scaled magnetic memory and room-temperature terahertz technologies. All-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions can display both a large TMR and a reciprocal switching effect, octupole-driven spin-transfer torque, enabling nanoscale magnetic memory and potentially room-temperature terahertz spintronic devices.
abstract_zh: 基于铁磁体的磁隧道结是自旋电子学中的典型器件，广泛应用于数据存储、计算和传感。它们通过隧道磁阻（TMR）1–5和自旋转移转矩6–9效应，分别实现磁序的电学检测和控制。长期以来，人们认为由于全反铁磁隧道结（AATJ）没有净磁化，这些效应都不可能显著。然而，最近的研究表明，基于手性反铁磁体的AATJ因其非相对论动量依赖自旋极化和团簇磁八极矩而表现出TMR，这些现象源于其自旋分裂的能带结构10–13。然而，互换效应，即自旋转移转矩的反铁磁对应体，因总电流是自旋中性而一直被认为不存在。在这里，我们报道了表现出这种互换效应的纳米级AATJ，我们称之为八极驱动自旋转移转矩（OTT）。我们演示了PtMn3|MgO|PtMn3 AATJ的电流诱导OTT开关，室温下TMR值为363%，开关电流密度约为10 MA cm–2。我们的理论模型从AATJ内亚和亚间自旋电流之间的不平衡解释了OTT的起源，并从每个PtMn3层非零净团簇八极极化这一等价角度进行了阐释。这项工作为反铁磁自旋电子学建立了新的材料平台，并为超规模磁存储和室温太赫兹技术提供了路径。所有反铁磁隧道结可以同时显示大TMR和互换开关效应——八极驱动自旋转移转矩，从而实现纳米级磁存储，并有望实现室温太赫兹自旋电子器件。
